provenance: Cold review of the ADR-033 resolver, 2026-08-24 (secondary finding: the refusal path). MEASURED RED at the first resolver: `extract_items(path, cover=True)` on a REFUSED document returned an envelope with NO `cover` key at all, because both refusal returns in extract.py sit above the block that built it -- while `boilerplate`, `tables` and `blocks` are all threaded into those same two returns by explicit design ('which still have readable text a caller who asked for chrome is entitled to'). ADR-033's ruling sentence says the flag 'adds one envelope key', unconditionally, and `envelope_shape` treats `cover` as optional, so nothing could catch the divergence. amended-cover-2021 is the fixture that makes the inconsistency indefensible: it is a 10-K/A, refused as out of scope by ADR-024, whose cover page is completely readable and whose registrant name resolves at full confidence. The behaviour pinned here is the one the other three annotation keys already have -- the key is present whenever the caller asked.
